key_insight: A minimal three-sphere model separates geometry- and friction-controlled particle trapping from fracture, with head-on impacts requiring lower fracture velocities at larger particle size ratios.
engineering_relevance: The model can help guide ball-milling impact conditions toward particle capture and breakage rather than ejection.
method: Simulate three-sphere collisions using the discrete element method (DEM).
Determine trapping with a closed-form geometric condition accounting for friction.
Evaluate fracture using Christensen-type stress and Weibull-type contact-force normalized criteria.
evidence_signal: DEM results show that particle outcomes and fracture thresholds depend on impact angle, obliquity, velocity, and particle size ratio.
watch_item: The reduced three-sphere model may not capture collective interactions in a full mill, and the abstract reports no experimental validation.
paper_title: Trapping and Fracture of Particles in Three-Sphere Ball-Milling Collisions
